
Robert Jordan uses several sources from mythology and history as inspiration for the character of Mat.

=={{Wiki|Odin}}==
[[File:Odin with spear.jpg|200px|thumb|Odin and his wolves depicted by Hans Thoma (1839-1924)]]

By far the most important source is the Norse God Odin. Odin is a war god, whereas Mat is one of the finest generals that ever lived. Like Mat, Odin is known by [[wikipedia:List of names of Odin|many names]], including "friend of wealth", "spear shaker/spearman", "one-eyed", "the one who is many", "swift tricker", "hanged one", "high one", "wayfinder", "god of wishes", "broad hat", "victory bringer" and many others which may be applicable to Mat's personality, plot arc or possessions. Several of the above allude to imagery common in depictions of Odin such as his wide-brimmed hat, long spear and one eye. "Wayfinder" refers to Mat's ability to always find a way out of a problem or more literally the finding of a long-lost ancient road during [[Knife of Dreams]]. "High One" is similar to the title afforded to him as the Prince of the Ravens, "Highness".{{ref/book|11|37}}

Odin was hanged for nine days on the a branch of the immense and sacred {{Wiki|Yggdrasil}}, also known as the Tree of Life, in exchange for knowledge. Mat is hanged on the legendary [[Avendesora]] and later explicitly tells Talmanes that "you could say I was-hanged for knowledge".{{Ref/book|6|5}} Later, [[Charlz Guybon]] mentions a rumour in [[Caemlyn]] about him being hanged for nine days.{{ref/book|13|19}} After he is hanged, he is given the [[Ashandarei|ashanderai]], a spear carved with two ravens and the inscription "thought is the arrow of time, memory never fades". Odin had two ravens, named Hugin and Munin: Thought and Memory. Where Odin's spear is magical, Mat's is Power-wrought. The second bargain Mat makes with the Eelfinn sees him giving up one of his eyes to pay for Moiraine's release. Odin sacrifices one of his eyes for "wisdom".

[[File:A901936284fa00b50b7f67fdd71f03c6.jpg|left|250px|thumb|Odin with his two ravens, Thought and Memory.]]In terms of personality, Mat loves female company and drinking and Odin is a famous womaniser and "requires no food, for wine is to him both meat and drink". He often sings song to himself and can speak the near-poetic Old Tongue where Odin is the god of poetry. Mat also has an excellent eye for horseflesh and enjoys the horse racing in Ebou Dar. Odin rides the eight-legged horse {{Wiki|Sleipnir}}, which is both a two-for-one bargain and bloody fast!

Lastly, Odin is a god of the dead. Mat's links with death are manifold; he dies twice and is brought back to life, he rescues Moiraine from her "death", he has a head filled with the memories of dead men and he causes the deaths of many, and will cause many more through his enabling of the invention of cannons. He is also linked, via the [[Horn of Valere]], to the dead heroes of legend who he called to battle. Odin presides over Valhalla, the hall of honored dead heroes who will fight at {{Wiki|Ragnarok}}, the Norse equivalent of the Last Battle.


==Tricksters==

Robert Jordan has been quoted in saying that Mat was influenced by trickster gods like Loki, Coyote and the Monkey King.<ref>Compuserve chat, 1996, Q13 [https://www.theoryland.com/intvmain.php?i=66]</ref> In general, there are few direct parallels between these and Mat, but all of them have a mischievous spirit, enjoy spinning tall tales and generally play the fool, while secretly being quite wily. All of these have obvious parallels with Mat's personality. 

===[[wikipedia:Coyote (mythology)|Coyote]]===
The indigenous North American character of Coyote is represented by Mat's connection with foxes through the Eelfinn, his medallion, and his ring. Mat is referred to in the [[Karaethon Cycle]] and by [[Lidya]]'s [[Foretelling]] as "the fox that makes the ravens fly," with the ravens representing the [[Seanchan]] in general or [[Tuon]] in particular. The fox is a creature of cunning in a wide range of literature from [[wikipedia:The Lion, the Bear and the Fox|Aesop's fables]] to {{Wiki|Reynard the Fox}} and [[wikipedia:Fantastic Mr. Fox|Roald Dahl]]. Coyote is also credited with stealing fire for humanity from supernatural being that were keeping it to themselves, paralleled by Mat's exposure of the secrets of the Illuminators' explosives through [[Aludra]] and [[Caemlyn]]'s bell founders.

===[[wikipedia:Raven Tales|Raven]]===
In North American cultures, the figure of Raven shares many of the same roles and stories as Coyote. Examples of Raven tales include "Raven steals fire", "Raven tries to marry a princess", "Raven Lost His Eyes," and "Raven kill Pitch Man." The last involves a man made of an amorphous material similar to the boneless ''[[gholam]]''. The obvious links to Mat are through the ravens engraved on his ''ashandarei'', that he married the heir to the Seanchan throne and the resulting title of Prince of Ravens, that he lost an eye in [[Sindhol]], the ravens on his signet ring, and his mortal defeat of the ''gholam''.<ref>phttps://www.theoryland.com/intvmain.php?i=580 Paris Signing Report, #12]</ref>

===The {{Wiki|Monkey King}}===

The Monkey King, known as Sun Wukong, is a mythological Chinese figure.

He is often depicted armed with his staff and is a formidable opponent, defeating a hundred thousand of the Army of Heaven in single combat. Mat is extremely proficient at the quarterstaff. He notably defeated both Gawyn and Galad while they wielded swords, shortly before both brothers became [[Blademasters]].

At the tactical and strategic scale, Mat defeated the Seanchan army with technology novel to the Third Age. The [[Fists of Heaven]] are part of the Seanchan army (which eventually fell under Mat's authority). Sun Wukong is also extremely fast, reportedly able to jump thousands of miles in a single leap, analogous to Mat's focus on speed and mobility as well as his use of Traveling. He <!-- Who is "he"? Monkey King? Or Mat? --> also claims to have learned all his skills and power from his dreams, which is true. Mat gained most of his skills from the memories of dead men inside his head, which often appear to him as dreamlike flashbacks.

=={{Wiki|Julius Caesar}}==

The parallels between Matrim Cauthon and Julius Caesar are largely militaristic in nature. {{Wiki|Julius Caesar}} is one of the most famous tacticians and generals in European history, if not world history, while Mat first established himself as a [[Five Great Captains|talented general]] following his encounter with the [[Finn|Aelfinn]] after passing through the [[twisted redstone doorframe]] in [[Rhuidean]]. Mat's supernatural military instinct eventually saw the formation of a private army loyal to Mat personally and named after the [[Band of the Red Hand]], an ancient band of Manetheren warriors. Likewise, the Roman legions that served under Julius Caesar during his [[Wikipedia:Gallic_Wars|Gallic campaigns]] were loyal to Caesar, ''not'' the Roman Republic.

A clear Caesar-Cauthon connection is in quotes regarding dice. Historical consensus puts the beginning of Caesar's Civil War at his [[wikipedia:Crossing_the_Rubicon#:~:text=According%20to%20Suetonius%2C%20Caesar%20uttered,the%20point%20of%20no%20return%22|crossing of the Rubicon River]] in northern Italy. The Roman historian Suetonius claims that before crossing the river - and officially violating Roman law - Julius Caesar uttered the now-famous line, "''ālea iacta est''" ("the die has been cast"). Matrim Cauthon occasionally uses the [[Old Tongue]] phrase "''Dovie'andi se tovya sagain''" ("time to toss the dice"). This phrase is eventually taken up by the Band of the Red Hand as a battle cry. The Old Tongue phrase is also on the new Band's [[Band_of_the_Red_Hand#Parallels|battle standard]].{{ref/book|6|5}}

Additionally, both Caesar and Mat are known womanizers. Caesar famously had affairs (and at least one illegitimate child) with multiple women, including [[wikipedia:Caesarion|Cleopatra]]. Mat had intimate relationships with numerous women throughout the series, including: [[Aludra Nendenhald]], an [[Illuminator]]; [[Tylin Quintara Mitsobar]], Queen of [[Altara]]; and of course [[Tuon Athaem Kore Paendrag|Fortuona Athaem Devi Paendrag]], Empress of the [[Seanchan]], whom he married.

== {{Wiki|Francis Marion}} ==

Like Mat, Francis Marion, an American revolutionary war hero, is associated with foxes (he was known as the Swamp Fox) and is known for waging successful guerilla campaigns against numerically superior forces, notably around [[Robert Jordan]]'s hometown.{{ref|Matrim Cauthon, Glossary, {{origins}}}}
